more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain cocoa and Chocolate products as covered by Directive 2000/36/EC; other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; fruit nectars as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable nectars and similar products; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.origin: Made by catalytic hydrogenation of neohesperidin. This is a chemically modified flavonoid preparation.
more_info.side_effects:
Reported food-use estimates were below the limit.
The assessment used an animal no-effect dose and an additional factor for limited-duration testing.
more_info.overview: Neohesperidin dihydrochalcone is a high-intensity sweetener obtained by catalytic hydrogenation of neohesperidin. It is used to strengthen an existing taste or aroma in the food. Made by catalytic hydrogenation of neohesperidin. This is a chemically modified flavonoid preparation. The specified material is supplied as off-white powder or crystalline material. It dissolves in hot water under the specified test conditions.
